scope: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both

section_map.heading: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both

claim_checks.claim: A transport is a "binding": it defines framing and delivery, not meaning; protocol semantics are the same on every transport
claim_checks.page_says: Protocol semantics are identical on every transport. A transport is a binding: it defines how messages are framed and delivered

claim_checks.claim: Two standard transports
claim_checks.page_says: The protocol currently defines two standard transport mechanisms for client-server communication
claim_checks.note: [24] also lists exactly stdio and Streamable HTTP.

claim_checks.claim: stdio. The client launches the server as a subprocess; messages are newline-delimited JSON-RPC on stdin/stdout and must not contain embedded newlines; the server may log to stderr and must write nothing else to stdout
claim_checks.page_says: Messages are delimited by newlines, and MUST NOT contain embedded newlines. … The server MUST NOT write anything to its stdout that is not a valid MCP message.

claim_checks.claim: Clients should support stdio whenever possible (2025-11-25 text)
claim_checks.page_says: Clients SHOULD support stdio whenever possible.

claim_checks.claim: In 2026-07-28 the server must not write JSON-RPC requests to stdout, cancellation is a `notifications/cancelled` message, and if the process dies the client should restart it and retry
claim_checks.page_says: the client SHOULD restart it. Because the protocol is stateless, any in-flight requests are simply lost and the client can retry them against the fresh process.
claim_checks.note: Stronger modal: the page makes restart a SHOULD but retry only permitted ('can retry'); the claim puts 'should' on both. The stdout and cancellation parts entail. Fix: 'the client should restart it and can retry the lost requests'. Role 3, so CRITICAL_FAIL at merge.

claim_checks.claim: Framing experiment (E1/E3): each message above was exactly one line, with the SDK server logging "server: ready" only on stderr
claim_checks.page_says: n/a: cites only local experiments

claim_checks.claim: Streamable HTTP. One MCP endpoint (for example `https://example.com/mcp`).
claim_checks.page_says: The server MUST provide a single HTTP endpoint path (hereafter referred to as the MCP endpoint) that supports POST. For example, this could be a URL like https://example.com/mcp.
claim_checks.note: example.com/mcp is an example URL, not a citation; its 'not fetched' status in sources.json does not matter.

claim_checks.claim: Client to server, 2025-11-25: every message is a new HTTP POST with `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`; body is one request, notification or response
claim_checks.page_says: listing both application/json and text/event-stream as supported content types. The body of the POST request MUST be a single JSON-RPC request, notification, or response.

claim_checks.claim: Client to server, 2026-07-28: POST of a single request or notification; clients must not POST responses; must send `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method` (and `Mcp-Name` for `tools/call`, `resources/read`, `prompts/get`)
claim_checks.page_says: The body of the HTTP POST MUST be a single JSON-RPC request or notification. The client MUST NOT send JSON-RPC responses. … These headers are REQUIRED for compliance.
claim_checks.note: The Standard Request Headers table names Mcp-Name for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get.

claim_checks.claim: Server reply to a request, 2025-11-25: `application/json` or `text/event-stream`
claim_checks.page_says: the server MUST either return Content-Type: text/event-stream, to initiate an SSE stream, or Content-Type: application/json, to return one JSON object.

claim_checks.claim: Server reply to a request, 2026-07-28: same
claim_checks.page_says: the server MUST return either Content-Type: application/json (a single JSON object) or Content-Type: text/event-stream (an SSE response stream).

claim_checks.claim: Notification accepted, 2025-11-25: 202, no body
claim_checks.page_says: If the server accepts the input, the server MUST return HTTP status code 202 Accepted with no body.

claim_checks.claim: Notification accepted, 2026-07-28: 202, no body
claim_checks.page_says: If the server accepts it, the server MUST return HTTP status code 202 Accepted with no body.

claim_checks.claim: Server-to-client channel, 2025-11-25: optional GET SSE stream; server may send requests on streams
claim_checks.page_says: The client MAY issue an HTTP GET to the MCP endpoint. … The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.

claim_checks.claim: Server-to-client channel, 2026-07-28: GET removed (405); no independent server requests; use MRTR and `subscriptions/listen`
claim_checks.page_says: HTTP GET or DELETE to the MCP endpoint: respond with 405 Method Not Allowed. … The server MUST NOT send independent JSON-RPC requests on this stream.
claim_checks.note: The 405 is a SHOULD for modern-only servers; the cell states no modal, so no overstatement.

claim_checks.claim: Sessions, 2025-11-25: optional `MCP-Session-Id`; 400 without it; 404 when ended; client `DELETE` to end
claim_checks.page_says: Servers that require a session ID SHOULD respond to requests without an MCP-Session-Id header (other than initialization) with HTTP 400 Bad Request.
claim_checks.note: 404 after termination is a MUST and DELETE is a client SHOULD on the same page. The cell compresses the 'servers that require a session ID' condition, which the word 'optional' covers.

claim_checks.claim: Sessions, 2026-07-28: none; a server should ignore an incoming `Mcp-Session-Id`
claim_checks.page_says: An Mcp-Session-Id header on a request: ignore it, and do not mint or echo session IDs.

claim_checks.claim: Resumability, 2025-11-25: SSE event ids and `Last-Event-ID`
claim_checks.page_says: it SHOULD issue an HTTP GET to the MCP endpoint, and include the Last-Event-ID header to indicate the last event ID it received.

claim_checks.claim: Resumability, 2026-07-28: not supported; a broken stream loses the request and the client re-sends it with a new id
claim_checks.page_says: Resumable SSE streams via Last-Event-ID are not supported. … A broken response stream loses the in-flight request; clients MUST re-issue it as a new request with a new request ID
claim_checks.note: The second quote is from [3] (changelog).

claim_checks.claim: Cancellation, 2025-11-25: explicit `notifications/cancelled`; a dropped connection is not a cancel
claim_checks.page_says: Disconnection SHOULD NOT be interpreted as the client cancelling its request. … To cancel, the client SHOULD explicitly send an MCP CancelledNotification.
claim_checks.note: The cited page names the message CancelledNotification, not the wire method name notifications/cancelled; same message.

claim_checks.claim: Cancellation, 2026-07-28: closing the response stream is the cancel
claim_checks.page_says: Closing the SSE response stream MUST be treated by the server as cancellation of that request.

claim_checks.claim: Origin check, 2025-11-25: server must validate `Origin`, 403 if invalid; local servers should bind to 127.0.0.1
claim_checks.page_says: If the Origin header is present and invalid, servers MUST respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden. … When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1)

claim_checks.claim: Origin check, 2026-07-28: same
claim_checks.page_says: Servers MUST validate the Origin header on all incoming connections to prevent DNS rebinding attacks. … servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1)

claim_checks.claim: Header/body check, 2025-11-25: version header on later requests; 400 on unsupported version
claim_checks.page_says: the client MUST include the MCP-Protocol-Version: <protocol-version> HTTP header on all subsequent requests … with an invalid or unsupported MCP-Protocol-Version, it MUST respond with 400 Bad Request

claim_checks.claim: Header/body check, 2026-07-28: headers are mirrored from the body; mismatch must be rejected with 400 and `-32020`
claim_checks.page_says: mirrors selected JSON-RPC body fields into HTTP headers … Servers MUST reject requests with a 400 Bad Request HTTP status and JSON-RPC error code -32020 (HeaderMismatch) if any validation fails.

claim_checks.claim: Custom headers, 2026-07-28: tool parameters marked `x-mcp-header` become `Mcp-Param-{Name}` headers; clients must support it
claim_checks.page_says: While the use of x-mcp-header is optional for servers, clients MUST support this feature. … construct the header name Mcp-Param-{name}

claim_checks.claim: Experiment E5 table (SDK 2.4.0 createMcpHandler): seven request/result rows
claim_checks.page_says: n/a: cites only local experiments

claim_checks.claim: The first six rows match the spec text
claim_checks.page_says: If the server does not implement the requested protocol version … it MUST respond with 400 Bad Request and an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError listing its supported versions.
claim_checks.note: Rows 2, 4, 5 and 6 match [13] directly (-32020 for mismatch and missing headers, 405 for GET). For row 3, [13] gives 400 plus an error that lists supported versions; the code -32022 itself appears only in [5]. Consider citing [5] beside [13].

claim_checks.claim: The last row is SDK behavior (dual-era fallback), which the spec permits for dual-era servers
claim_checks.page_says: A server that wishes to support both legacy clients (which expect an initialize handshake) and modern clients (which use per-request metadata) MAY implement both behaviors.

claim_checks.claim: Experiment E6 (SDK 1.32.2, legacy sessions over real HTTP on 127.0.0.1): session id, 202, 400, DELETE 200, 404
claim_checks.page_says: n/a: cites only local experiments

claim_checks.claim: This matches the 2025-11-25 session rules
claim_checks.page_says: The server MAY terminate the session at any time, after which it MUST respond to requests containing that session ID with HTTP 404 Not Found.
claim_checks.note: Session ID at initialize (MAY), 202 for the notification, 400 without the id (SHOULD) and client DELETE (SHOULD) are all on the same page.

claim_checks.claim: HTTP+SSE is the transport of the 2024-11-05 revision. Streamable HTTP was introduced in 2025-03-26 as its replacement
claim_checks.page_says: Streamable HTTP was introduced in protocol version 2025-03-26 as a replacement for the HTTP+SSE transport from protocol version 2024-11-05.

claim_checks.claim: It is formally Deprecated (registry, SEP-2596): deprecated since 2025-03-26, new implementations should not adopt it, migrate to Streamable HTTP
claim_checks.page_says: deprecated since protocol version 2025-03-26 and is classified as Deprecated under the feature lifecycle policy (SEP-2596). New implementations SHOULD NOT adopt it; existing implementations SHOULD migrate to Streamable HTTP.
claim_checks.note: Quote from [13]; the [21] registry row agrees (SEP-2596, 2025-03-26, Streamable HTTP).

claim_checks.claim: It is "eligible for removal in a future revision"; the registry says earliest removal is "Three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final"
claim_checks.page_says: HTTP+SSE transport | SEP-2596 | 2025-03-26 | Streamable HTTP | Three months after SEP-2596 reaches Final … The earliest removal marks when a feature becomes eligible for removal
claim_checks.note: The substance holds on [21]. But the first quoted phrase is copied word for word from [13], not from [21], which the bullet does not cite. Add [13] to this bullet.

claim_checks.claim: No feature has been removed yet
claim_checks.page_says: No features have been removed under this policy yet.
claim_checks.note: Dropped qualifier 'under this policy'. Without it the claim is wider than the page and clashes with the doc's own text: 3.1 says 2026-07-28 removed the GET stream, sessions and resumability. Fix: 'No feature has been removed under the SEP-2596 lifecycle policy yet'. Role 5, so CRITICAL_FAIL at merge.

claim_checks.claim: Backward-compat probe (both eras): POST a request to the URL; if it fails with 400, 404 or 405 (and in 2026-07-28 the body is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error), GET the URL expecting an SSE stream whose first event is `endpoint`; if so, use the old transport
claim_checks.page_says: If it fails with HTTP status code 400 Bad Request, 404 Not Found, or 405 Method Not Allowed and the response body is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error
claim_checks.note: [4] gives the same probe without the body condition, using an InitializeRequest.

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: stdio: send `server/discover` first. A `DiscoverResult` or a recognized modern error means modern; any other error or a timeout means legacy, so fall back to `initialize`. Do not key the fallback to one error code
claim_checks.page_says: The fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one specific error code … The server returns any other error, or does not respond within a reasonable timeout: the server is legacy.

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: HTTP: send a modern request; on a 400, read the body; a recognized modern error means modern (retry), anything else means legacy
claim_checks.page_says: the client SHOULD inspect the response body before falling back … If the body is empty or is not a recognized modern JSON-RPC error, fall back to initialize

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: Cache the answer per process (stdio) or origin (HTTP)
claim_checks.page_says: Clients SHOULD cache the result for the lifetime of the server process (stdio) or origin (HTTP)

claim_checks.section: ### 3.3 Era detection for clients that must support both
claim_checks.claim: Compatibility matrix highlights: modern client against legacy server fails; legacy client against modern-only server fails; dual-era implementations on either side work
claim_checks.page_says: Modern | Legacy | Fails. … Legacy | Modern | Fails. … Dual-era | Legacy | Works. … Legacy | Dual-era | Works.

claim_checks.claim: Row 'Server runs on the user's machine, launched by the host' -> stdio. Why: no network surface; spec says local servers should use stdio to limit access to the client
claim_checks.page_says: SHOULD implement measures to prevent unauthorized usage from malicious processes: … Use the stdio transport to limit access to just the MCP client … Restrict access if using an HTTP transport
claim_checks.note: The SHOULD applies to 'implement measures'. Stdio is one listed measure, beside a restricted HTTP transport, so 'local servers should use stdio' overstates. 'No network surface' is the doc's inference, not page text. Fix: 'spec lists stdio as one way to limit access to just the client'. Role 6, so SOFT_WARN.

claim_checks.claim: Same row: credentials come from the environment, not OAuth
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.

claim_checks.claim: Row 'Shared or remote server, many users' -> Streamable HTTP + OAuth. Why: single endpoint, works through ordinary HTTP infrastructure; load balancers can route on `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` headers
claim_checks.page_says: mirrors selected JSON-RPC body fields into HTTP headers so that intermediaries (load balancers, gateways, observability tooling) can route and inspect requests without parsing the body.

claim_checks.claim: Row 'Local HTTP server' -> Streamable HTTP bound to 127.0.0.1, validate `Origin`, require a token
claim_checks.page_says: When running locally, servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1) … Require an authorization token … Servers MUST validate the Origin header

claim_checks.claim: Row 'Existing HTTP+SSE server' -> keep old endpoints only for old clients, add Streamable HTTP
claim_checks.page_says: Continue to host both the SSE and POST endpoints of the old transport, alongside the new “MCP endpoint” defined for the Streamable HTTP transport.

claim_checks.claim: Row 'Need server push of tool-list changes' -> `subscriptions/listen` (2026-07-28) or GET stream (legacy)
claim_checks.page_says: toolsListChanged | boolean | Receive notifications/tools/list_changed when tools change … The server MAY send JSON-RPC requests and notifications on the stream.

claim_checks.claim: Scope. Authorization is optional. HTTP implementations should follow the spec; stdio implementations should not, and should read credentials from the environment
claim_checks.page_says: Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations. … Implementations using an HTTP-based transport SHOULD conform to this specification. … STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.

claim_checks.claim: Alternative transports must follow established best practice for their protocol
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using alternative transports MUST follow established security best practices for their protocol.
claim_checks.note: Dropped qualifier: 'security best practices' written as 'best practice', which widens the MUST to all best practice. Fix: 'must follow established security best practices for their protocol'. Role 3, so CRITICAL_FAIL at merge.

claim_checks.claim: Roles. The MCP server is an OAuth 2.1 resource server; the MCP client is an OAuth 2.1 client; the authorization server issues tokens and may be separate from the MCP server
claim_checks.page_says: A protected MCP server acts as an OAuth 2.1 resource server … It may be hosted with the resource server or a separate entity.
claim_checks.note: The page says 'a protected MCP server'. Here the context (authorization for HTTP servers, authorization optional) keeps the meaning. Optional wording fix: 'A protected MCP server'.

claim_checks.claim: Flow (steps are normative unless marked), with step 1: client calls with no token; server returns 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="..."` (and optionally `scope="..."`)
claim_checks.page_says: MCP servers MUST implement one of the following discovery mechanisms … Include the resource metadata URL in the WWW-Authenticate HTTP header under resource_metadata when returning 401 Unauthorized responses
claim_checks.note: Step 1 has no mark of its own and is grounded under the Flow mark. It shows only the header route, which is one of two allowed mechanisms; step 2 states the either/or correctly, so it is not flagged. A scope in the challenge is a server SHOULD in [26]; 'optionally' understates it, which is not a violation.

claim_checks.claim: 2. Client fetches the Protected Resource Metadata (RFC 9728), which must list at least one entry in `authorization_servers`. Servers must support either the header or the well-known URI (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/path]`); clients must support both, header first
claim_checks.page_says: containing at least one authorization server. … MCP clients MUST support both discovery mechanisms and use the resource metadata URL from the parsed WWW-Authenticate headers when present

claim_checks.claim: 3. Client discovers authorization server metadata, trying RFC 8414 and OpenID Connect well-known URLs in a fixed priority order, and must reject metadata whose `issuer` differs from the issuer used to build the URL
claim_checks.page_says: the issuer value in the document MUST be identical to the issuer identifier used to construct the well-known URL. If they differ, the client MUST NOT use the metadata.

claim_checks.claim: 4. Client obtains a client id. Priority for clients that support all: pre-registered credentials, then Client ID Metadata Documents (an HTTPS URL as `client_id`, if the server advertises `client_id_metadata_document_supported`), then Dynamic Client Registration, then prompt the user
claim_checks.page_says: Clients supporting all options SHOULD use the following priority order: … Use Dynamic Client Registration as a fallback if the Authorization Server supports it
claim_checks.note: The 'server' that advertises CIMD support is the authorization server, per the page.

claim_checks.claim: Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated in 2026-07-28
claim_checks.page_says: Dynamic Client Registration | PR #2858 | 2026-07-28 | Client ID Metadata Documents … Dynamic Client Registration is deprecated.

claim_checks.claim: 5. Client runs authorization code flow with PKCE (`S256`); it must verify the server advertises `code_challenge_methods_supported` and refuse to continue otherwise
claim_checks.page_says: the S256 code challenge method when technically capable … If code_challenge_methods_supported is absent, the authorization server does not support PKCE and MCP clients MUST refuse to proceed.
claim_checks.note: S256 is a MUST 'when technically capable'. The claim's '(S256)' states no modal, so it is not flagged; adding the qualifier would make it exact.

claim_checks.claim: 6. Both authorization and token requests must include the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter naming the MCP server's canonical URI, whether or not the authorization server supports it
claim_checks.page_says: MUST be included in both authorization requests and token requests. … MCP clients MUST send this parameter regardless of whether authorization servers support it.

claim_checks.claim: 7. Client records the authorization server `issuer` before redirecting and checks the `iss` parameter on the response (RFC 9207) before sending the code anywhere
claim_checks.page_says: Before redirecting the user-agent, the client MUST record the issuer value … MCP clients MUST apply the validation in RFC9207 Section 2.4 before transmitting the authorization code to any token endpoint

claim_checks.claim: 8. Client sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every HTTP request; tokens must not go in the query string
claim_checks.page_says: Note that authorization MUST be included in every HTTP request from client to server. … Access tokens MUST NOT be included in the URI query string

claim_checks.claim: 9. Server must validate the token and that it was issued for this server as audience; invalid or expired gives `401`; insufficient scope gives `403` with `error="insufficient_scope"` and a `scope` listing what the operation needs
claim_checks.page_says: Invalid or expired tokens MUST receive an HTTP 401 response. … the server SHOULD respond with: … HTTP 403 Forbidden status code … error="insufficient_scope"
claim_checks.note: The 403 challenge contents are a SHOULD and the 401 is a MUST; the claim states no modal for either.

claim_checks.claim: 10. Step-up: the client unions previously requested scopes with the challenged scopes, re-authorizes, and retries a limited number of times
claim_checks.page_says: Determine required scopes by computing the union of the client’s previously requested scope set and the scopes from the current challenge. … no more than a few times

claim_checks.claim: Scope selection at first authorization: use the `scope` from the `WWW-Authenticate` header if present; otherwise all `scopes_supported` from the resource metadata; otherwise omit `scope`
claim_checks.page_says: Use scope parameter from the initial WWW-Authenticate header in the 401 response, if provided … use all scopes defined in scopes_supported … omitting the scope parameter if scopes_supported is undefined

claim_checks.claim: Refresh tokens: clients must keep them confidential and must not assume they will be issued; servers should not put `offline_access` in their challenges or `scopes_supported`
claim_checks.page_says: MUST keep refresh tokens confidential in transit and storage … MUST NOT assume refresh tokens will be issued … SHOULD NOT include offline_access in WWW-Authenticate scope or Protected Resource Metadata scopes_supported

claim_checks.claim: The 2026-07-28 changelog confirms the `iss` addition and the DCR deprecation
claim_checks.page_says: MCP clients MUST validate a present iss against the recorded issuer before redeeming the authorization code (SEP-2468). … Deprecate the OAuth 2.0 Dynamic Client Registration Protocol (RFC7591)

claim_checks.claim: Local stdio server: no OAuth; pass secrets by environment variable or config
claim_checks.page_says: Implementations using an STDIO transport SHOULD NOT follow this specification, and instead retrieve credentials from the environment.
claim_checks.note: Wider scope: the page names only the environment; 'or config' is not on the cited page. Fix: 'pass secrets by environment variable' (or cite a source for config files). Role 6, so SOFT_WARN.

claim_checks.claim: Public or enterprise remote server, unknown clients: OAuth 2.1 + PKCE + Protected Resource Metadata + `resource` parameter; accept Client ID Metadata Documents; keep Dynamic Client Registration only for old authorization servers
claim_checks.page_says: Authorization servers and MCP clients SHOULD support OAuth Client ID Metadata Documents … retained for backwards compatibility with authorization servers that do not support Client ID Metadata Documents.
claim_checks.note: PKCE is required in [29], which this row does not cite; [26] refers to the PKCE code verifier and requires following Security Considerations.

claim_checks.claim: Known client and server relationship: pre-registered client id
claim_checks.page_says: Pre-registration: When client and server have an existing relationship

claim_checks.claim: Server calls third-party APIs for the user: server runs its own OAuth client to the third party (URL-mode elicitation to get the user there); never forward the MCP token
claim_checks.page_says: URL mode elicitation enables a pattern where MCP servers act as OAuth clients to third-party resource servers. … The MCP server MUST NOT use the client’s credentials for the third-party service

claim_checks.claim: Server acts as an OAuth proxy with a static client id to a third party: per-client consent before forwarding, exact `redirect_uri` match, `state` checks
claim_checks.page_says: MCP proxy servers MUST implement per-client consent and proper security controls … Use exact string matching (not pattern matching or wildcards) … Reject any callback requests where the state parameter is missing

claim_checks.claim: Local HTTP server: bind 127.0.0.1, validate `Origin`, require a token or use a Unix socket
claim_checks.page_says: Require an authorization token … Use unix domain sockets or other Interprocess Communication (IPC) mechanisms with restricted access … servers SHOULD bind only to localhost (127.0.0.1)
